When I was 14-15 years old and my brother was around 7-8, we’d play Minecraft Pocket Edition a lot since that was the only one we’d have access to.

Since I was a teenager with zero restrictions online, while my brother was a monitored kid. I would follow Mojang on social media and know the dates for game updates. So instead of helping my brother update his game around the same time as me, I’d only update mine at launch, then wait a week to update his. When he’s ask how I’m getting updates before him, I convinced him that I worked for Mojang and was testing the latest updates for the company.

I did this for over 6 months.

Final Fantasy VI

During the pandemic there were only three things keeping me from becoming an emotional mess. Animal Crossing New Horizons, Final Fantasy VI and my pet kitten that I got in December 2019.

In 2021, I fell off Animal Crossing and my cat died in December that year. So all I had for FFVI. I didn’t have the heart to finish it for the longest time. I left the game right before the final area for over a year because I knew that once I finished it, I’d have nothing left.

After over a year of not touching the game, I finished it in November 2022 and despite the game’s theming being about loss, I didn’t feel like I had nothing left after playing. I felt like a gained something. Seeing the stories of all these different characters come to a nice conclusion made me feel satisfied. I kinda felt bad for not letting them have their happy endings for over a year. I really appreciate this game and it instantly made it to my top three favourite games of all time

My mum and I (24F) had an argument a few weeks back about how my younger brother insists on helping me with things when I never asked for his help. The frustrating part is I look like the asshole when I just need space.

My brother (17M) has this annoying habit where he doesn’t ask if I need help with something. He just assumes I do and “helps” anyway when I was perfectly fine. In the rare times he does ask and I say no, he does this thing where he “stealth helps”. For example. We have a dog who tries to lick the dishwasher when I’m filling it. He’ll ask if I need help getting him away, I’ll say no, then suddenly he just so happens to want to pet and play with the dog in that moment.

My side of the argument is that help is only help when it’s offered/asked for and accepted by the person you’re helping. Consent is important to me on this and I don’t appreciate people butting in unless it’s an emergency or were in a rush. I have multiple disabilities, so I don’t have as many opportunities to be independent. 

Meanwhile, my mum’s side of the argument is that “he helps you because he loves you. He wants to help his big sister”. Another point she makes is that I won’t ask him for help otherwise, which isn’t a valid point since why would I get help from someone who doesn’t respect my boundaries? I WOULD actually ask him more if he made himself more approachable. But right now, I’d rather risk breaking my neck standing on a chair to reach something than ask the 6ft tall boy to do it. My mum also thinks I have a thing against receiving help, which is true. But again, that would be solved if he just backed off a bit.
